subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Dining Car Revolution
description: A quick, practical guide to The Dining Car Revolution.

hook.text: Early passengers packed their own food or grabbed bites at station stops lasting five minutes.

buildup.text: In 1868, Pullman added the first dining car with a full kitchen cooking meals on board.

discovery.text: Passengers could eat a hot steak dinner at 60 mph while watching the countryside roll by.

twist.text: Dining cars never turned a profit. They were loss leaders designed to lure passengers to rail.

climax.text: Airlines later copied the idea with in-flight meals—but trains did it first and better.

punchline.text: The dining car sold the journey, not the destination.

quiz.question: Why did railways run dining cars despite losing money?
options: They attracted passengers to choose rail travel
